question: India has been a World Trade Organization (WTO) member since _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India became a member of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** on **1 January 1995**, following the ratification of the Marrakesh Agreement.
 
• The **World Trade Organization (WTO)** was established on **1 January 1995**, replacing the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** which had been in effect since 1948.
 
• India was one of the founding members of the WTO and has actively participated in its negotiations and functions. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• The WTO aims to facilitate international trade, reduce trade barriers, and provide a platform for trade negotiations and dispute resolution.
 
• India's membership in the WTO has had a significant impact on its **trade policies**, leading to liberalization and greater integration into the global economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):**

 
 
• The WTO is an intergovernmental organization that regulates international trade. It currently has **164 member countries**.
 
• It was established to replace the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**, which was created in 1948.
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement, signed in **April 1994**, led to the establishment of the WTO.
 
 
 
• **India’s involvement in the WTO:**
 
 
• India is a founding member of the WTO and has played a crucial role in advocating for the interests of **developing countries**.
 
• India has actively participated in the WTO’s **Doha Development Round**, focusing on issues like agricultural subsidies, trade facilitation, and special treatment for developing nations.
 
• India has also used the WTO’s dispute resolution mechanism to address trade issues and protect its interests.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the WTO:**
 
 
• The WTO provides a framework for negotiating trade agreements and a dispute resolution mechanism to enforce participants' adherence to its agreements.
 
• It aims to reduce trade barriers and ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• The WTO also monitors and reviews trade policies of member countries and provides technical assistance to developing countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between GATT and WTO:**

 
 
• **GATT** was a set of rules, while the **WTO** is a permanent organization with a more comprehensive framework.
 
• The WTO includes trade in services and intellectual property, which were not covered under GATT.
 
• The WTO has a stronger **dispute resolution mechanism** compared to GATT.
 
 
 
• **India’s Trade Liberalization:**
 
 
• India’s WTO membership has led to reforms in its **foreign trade policies**, including reduction in tariffs and export subsidies.
 
• India has benefited from WTO initiatives like **special and differential treatment** provisions for developing countries.
 
• Despite challenges, India continues to advocate for the interests of **developing and least-developed countries** within the WTO framework.
